s1.syndrome_frame: A subacute to chronic, asymptomatic, solitary skin lesion
salient_findings: Single asymptomatic lesion on the dorsum of the left hand
Lesion gradually increased in size over 10 months
key_facts: 42-year-old woman
Lesion located on the dorsal aspect of the left hand
Lesion size: 4 × 3 cm
Lesion is firm and non-tender
Lesion is not adherent to the overlying skin
No history of trauma, discharge, pain, redness, bleeding, or restriction of joint movement
No regional lymphadenopathy
Routine hematologic, liver, and renal function tests are within normal limits

differentials: Giant cell tumor of tendon sheath
per_call: Giant cell tumor of tendon sheath

shortlist.label: Dermatofibroma
shortlist.why_kept: Common, benign skin tumor matching the description of a firm, non-tender nodule

shortlist.label: Lipoma
shortlist.why_kept: Benign tumor of fat cells, possible given the lesion's size and location

shortlist.label: Epidermoid cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Common, benign cyst that could present as a firm, non-tender nodule

shortlist.label: Dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans
shortlist.why_kept: Rare, malignant tumor that could present similarly, important to consider for diagnosis

shortlist.label: Keloid
shortlist.why_kept: Benign growth that could match the description, especially given the lesion's size and location

raw.rationale: The lesion is a solitary, firm, non-tender nodule that is not adherent to the overlying skin, which is consistent with the characteristics of a dermatofibroma.

rejected.label: Lipoma
rejected.why: Lipomas are typically soft and mobile, which does not match the firm nature of the lesion.

rejected.label: Epidermoid cyst
rejected.why: Epidermoid cysts are often fluctuant and may have a visible punctum, which is not described in the case.

rejected.label: Dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans
rejected.why: Dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans is a rare malignant tumor that typically presents with a larger, more irregular lesion and may have a history of growth or ulceration, which is not consistent with the case.

rejected.label: Keloid
rejected.why: Keloids are typically found at sites of previous trauma and are often pruritic or tender, which does not match the asymptomatic nature of the lesion.
